name: Split header-word completion
mechanism: Positions complete the trailing piece of a word split across tokens in numbered section headers and all-caps category tags (7Sh->opping, 3Enter->tainment, HOT->EL, FER->RY); the a6/a9 PCA directions appear to carry the word-prefix identity forward to finish the label.

name: Listing-field continuation
mechanism: Positions are the next element inside a directory entry: street-name words (' St', ' Court'), second halves of address ranges (257-259), second words of proper names, and the newline closing a map-key line, suggesting these components track position within the entry template.

name: Section headings and postcodes
mechanism: Positions complete standard section-heading words (Eating/Sleeping/Shopping) and the newline right after them, plus the digit of London postcodes (WC2, NW1), i.e. highly predictable slots in the listing boilerplate.

name: TOC place-name items
mechanism: Positions predict the next place-name item in '####' table-of-contents runs (#### Rye, #### Sandwich, Marg->ate) and map-grid coordinates after venue names (AudioF4), i.e. items in enumerated index lists.

name: Index-entry label completion
mechanism: Across map-key and review entries, positions complete all-caps category tags (BOOK->S, CL->UB), grid references (F3, D2), and numbered header words; layer-9 attention heads plus a6 directions look like the machinery that recognizes and continues these index labels.

name: Contact-line digits and separators
mechanism: Positions are digits and punctuation inside listing metadata lines: phone-number chunks (%01227-78'77'), postcode digits, grid references, and the semicolons that separate fields, i.e. the formulaic contact/address string format.

name: Price and ticket fields
mechanism: Positions follow the stock admission/rate templates of listings: 'adult/' -> child/family, 's/d' -> ' from' before a price, phone digits, and quantity words before pound amounts, so the components appear to implement the price-field grammar.

name: Listing-entry boundary structure
mechanism: A large parent cluster over the whole listing format: newlines that terminate entries and category tags (PUB\n, CAFE\n), standard heading-word completions, and closing punctuation, with mid-layer heads (6.0, 7.8) and a17/m7 marking where one entry ends and the next begins.

name: Caps category-tag endings
mechanism: Positions complete all-caps venue category tags (NEIGHBOURH->OOD, TOUR, MODERN EUROPEAN) and the newline immediately after the tag, i.e. the end of the 'Name + CATEGORY' review-header pattern.

name: All-caps tag completion
mechanism: Positions finish split all-caps category tags (PU->B, THEAT->RE, HOST->EL, LANDM->ARK, BRIT->ISH) and split proper names (Gat->wick, Marg->ate); a7/a17 directions seem to hold the partial-word state needed to complete the tag.

name: Standard heading-word prediction
mechanism: Positions predict the canonical guidebook heading word after '####' or a numbered prefix (Sights, Eating, Tours, Information, Entertainment) and second words of sight names in indexes, i.e. choosing which stock section title comes next.

name: Repeated venue-name recall
mechanism: Positions complete venue names in 'A'-bulleted best-of lists (AG->oring, AK->oya, ALed->bury) and heading/entry newlines, which looks like copying names already seen elsewhere in the guide plus generic heading structure; the mix is real, so confidence is limited.

name: Entry-terminating newline
mechanism: Nearly every position is the newline that closes a numbered map-key or TOC line, right after a grid coordinate or place name; the components appear to detect that the entry is complete and emit the line break.

name: Multi-word landmark completion
mechanism: Positions are the second word of familiar multi-word proper names in numbered indexes (Westminster Abbey, Clarence House, Heron Tower, Hoxton Hotel), so m7/a7 directions look like they retrieve the known continuation of a named entity.

name: Numeric metadata fields
mechanism: Positions are numbers and stock phrases inside listing metadata: 'r/d from' before prices, population figures (Pop 151,200), opening-hour tokens (4pm), and street numbers, i.e. the numeric slots of the listing template.

name: Mixed residual continuations
mechanism: A heterogeneous mix of split-word completions (Cy->cling, MUS->IC), grid references, and ordinary prose function words (' then', ' have', ' of') with no single common function beyond generic guidebook continuation; likely a residual slice of the parent cluster.

name: Paragraph-final newline
mechanism: The dominant positions are the newline after a sentence-ending period that closes a paragraph before a new heading, mixed with some caps category-tag endings; head 17.8 and m7 directions appear to signal paragraph/entry closure.
